subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out the dimensions for a six-wheeled carrier vehicle - body length, wheel positions, hull shape, cab, and a railgun mounted on the rear deck, aiming for a compact but detailed design.

Now I'm planning the mechanical structure: a turret with the barrel pointing forward over the cab, deployable outrigger legs with hydraulic hinges for stability, and a joint hierarchy connecting the chassis, wheels, turret, and legs, plus surface details like panel textures, decals, and hazard stripes to add visual richness.

Working out wheel placement, fender guards, and hull geometry...

Now for the cab and railgun turret: I'm positioning the windscreen and visor, then figuring out the gun's yaw/pitch joints. I realize it's simpler to build the gun pointing straight along +Z unposed, then apply pitch rotation afterward rather than posing before building, since parts land in whatever frame they're built in.

Raising the trunnion to y 3.3 avoids collision with the cab roof, and the slight downward elevation still clears the barrel over the hull at full extension. Now I'm laying out the twin rail boxes, breech block, capacitor drums, coil rings, muzzle, recoil rods, and cradle plates, along with the turret yaw drum dimensions.

For stability I'm placing four outrigger legs between the wheel positions at roughly z=1.7 and z=-1.3 on both sides, each with a hinge joint, an angled outward arm, and a vertical piston leading to a ground pad.

Adding foot joints aimed downward and verifying floor contact for pads and wheel hubs. I'm settling on materials now—a mottled olive panel for the hull, dark steel trim, yellow accents, cyan glow, and matte black tyres—making sure the paint/texture approach works with the box geometry normals.

Now I'm planning decals and detail elements: a hex-chevron emblem on hull and cab, hazard stripe texture on the leg pads, a "RG-6" unit number, plus antenna whip, light bar, smoke launchers, tow hook, exhaust stacks, side fuel drums, ammo crates, glowing headlights, and a rear tow bar. I'm setting up helper functions for boxes and cylinders attached to bones before writing the actual part-placement code.

Writing wheel geometry...

Checking that the hull and wheel positions don't clash, I adjust the hull half-width down to 1.25 so tyres sit at 1.35-1.85 without excessive total width, bringing it to a more reasonable 2.5 wide chassis. Now I'm sketching the upper deck and cab placement above the hull.

Still placing cab geometry...

I need to add a glow gap bar between the rails and figure out capacitor drum placement relative to the cheeks, repositioning the cheeks wider so the drums can sit inside them without overlap.

Coil rings using toruses facing along the z-axis will encircle the rail barrel in a repeating pattern, spaced out to form a coil gun look, with a muzzle shroud box capping the front and recoil damper rods connecting back to the cheeks. I'm attaching this whole rail assembly to the pitch joint with a trunnion rod and setting pitch to -8 degrees before moving on to the leg structure.

Now I'm adding deployed legs (four), ammo crates stacked behind the turret with hazard markings, side tool boxes, rear exhaust stacks rising near the cab, antenna whips, and a rotating radar dish on the roof. I'll also work in a name tag decal reading "RG-6" on the gun side and hazard-stripe SVG texturing for the leg sleeve.

Writing leg joint code...

Still adding more parts...
